President Bola Tinubu has commended the Oba of Benin, Omo N’Oba N’Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo Ewuare II, for advocating the return of looted Benin artefacts.
Mr Tinubu, represented by the Minister of Regional Development, Abubakar Momoh, gave the commendation at the traditional ruler’s 10th coronation anniversary reception on Saturday in Benin.
He also praised the Oba for promoting peace and unity across Nigeria.
Mr Tinubu said history remained a living presence in Edo, reflected in the throne, language, festivals and achievements of the Benin people.
According to him, the Benin Kingdom represents organised government, diplomacy and excellence rooted in its history.
The president also commended the traditional ruler’s opposition to human trafficking, describing it as a traditional institution’s response to contemporary challenges.
He called for greater cooperation between relevant institutions and the palace to ensure the full recovery of the looted artefacts.

Also speaking, Governor Monday Okpebholo congratulated the Oba, saying his decade on the throne reflected commitment to preserving Benin’s cultural heritage.
“This anniversary is not merely a celebration of time spent on the throne; it is also an opportunity to reflect on the enduring responsibility of preserving the values of the kingdom,” he said.
The governor prayed for continued peace, wisdom, unity and progress during the traditional ruler’s reign.
He expressed hope that relations between the palace, Edo State Government and the people would strengthen through mutual respect and cooperation.
On the Museum of West African Arts, Mr Okpebholo announced its renaming as the Benin Royal Palace Museum of West African Arts.
He said the inclusion of the Royal Palace recognised its role as custodian of the kingdom’s history, traditions and heritage.
“Our history must not only be preserved; it must be properly documented, celebrated and transmitted to generations yet unborn,” he added.
The Oba thanked dignitaries from the federal and Edo governments, diplomatic corps, his queens and subjects for attending the celebration.
He particularly appreciated the Sultan of Sokoto, Muhammad Abubakar, for attending after another engagement in Ibadan.
“This is not a time for speech making but a time for merriment and rejoicing to the glory of God,” the Oba said.
The News Agency of Nigeria recalls that the anniversary celebration began on 3 October and ended with the grand reception.
Other dignitaries included the Emir of Kagara, Ahmad Gunna; Edo Deputy Governor Dennis Idahosa, and Norwegian Ambassador, Svein Bæra.
The Minister of Art, Culture and Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, was also among the dignitaries.
